title: Operations Concierge Playbook: Access, Change, Procurement & Travel
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates our standard operating procedures for employee access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expense approvals, vendor onboarding, and employee travel. It is designed as a single "concierge" reference for stakeholders who coordinate cross-functional approvals and execution (line managers, people-ops, finance, security, and legal).

Principles
- Least privilege: Grant only the minimum access required for a task and review quarterly.
- Clear accountability: Every request must have a named approver and an operational owner.
- Auditability: Decisions, approvals, and evidence (receipts, contracts, IAM logs) must be retained per retention rules.
- Risk-tiered control: Higher value / sensitive activities require stricter review and formal sign-off.

1) Access & Permissions Lifecycle
Intro: Applies to all access requests for cloud consoles, production systems, data stores, internal tools, and third-party SaaS.

Request flow (standard):
1. Submit request through Access Portal (Confluence link + internal form). Include: justification, duration, resources, data categories.
2. Manager approval (explicit) within 72 hours.
3. Security review for requests involving sensitive or regulated data (PII, PHI, PCI).
4. IAM provisioning & automation executes change; owner confirms access.
5. Scheduled review dates added (default 90 days) with auto-expiration.

Emergency access flow (break glass):
- Owner submits an emergency ticket in PagerDuty with category "BreakGlass" and tags the security oncall.
- Temporary access granted for a maximum of 12 hours, logged and must be reconciled with a post-incident justification within 24 hours.

Permission Tiers and Approvals:
- Tier 1 (non-sensitive tooling, read-only): manager approval.
- Tier 2 (write access to production-adjacent infra): manager + platform lead.
- Tier 3 (access to PII/regulated systems, production writes): manager + security + legal where contract/regulatory scope applies.

Required evidence and logging:
- Request form copy, approval chain, policy link, IAM ticket id, and audit log export (CSV) uploaded to the ticket before closure.

2) Change Management (software + infra)
Scope: Applies to changes that modify runtime behavior, data schemas, deployments, infra configuration, or access patterns.

Change categories:
- Standard (pre-approved routine ops): follow runbook, update change log.
- Minor (low risk): RFC + reviewer signoff; can be scheduled in maintenance window.
- Major (high risk, data migration, schema change, infra reconfiguration): full RFC, cross-team review, dry run in staging, canary rollout plan, rollback procedure.
- Emergency: declared by oncall; must be postmortem'd and converted into a formal RFC within 72 hours.

Change approval matrix (example):
- <= $500 infra spend & non-customer facing: team lead
- $500–$5,000 or schema changes affecting <1% of users: infra manager + SRE
- > $5,000 or customer-impacting: infra manager + SRE + Product + Finance (if budgetary)

Rollout & rollback:
- All major changes require documented canary metrics, automated health checks, and a single-button rollback where possible.
- If a rollback is executed, follow the Incident Report template and schedule an RCA within 3 business days.

Change window guidance:
- Default maintenance window: Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC.
- Exceptions must be approved 72 hours in advance and include a fallback plan.

3) Data Management & Classification
Classification levels:
- Public: safe to publish. Retention: optional.
- Internal: non-sensitive internal use. Retention: 1 year unless otherwise noted.
- Confidential: business-sensitive (contracts, roadmaps). Retention: 3 years.
- Regulated: PII, PHI, PCI. Retention and handling per legal/regulatory requirements; encrypt at rest & in transit.

Handling rules:
- Regulated data must be stored in approved encrypted stores (KMS-backed) and access limited to Tier 3.
- De-identification is required before data leaves secure environments for analysis.
- Backups: encryption enabled; retention schedules must be documented and reviewed annually.

Data retention & deletion schedule (summary table):
- Logs (system): 90 days raw, 1 year aggregated
- Audit trails (access): 3 years
- Employee records: 7 years post-employment
- Vendor contracts: 7 years after contract end

4) Procurement & Expense Approval Patterns
Spending thresholds and approvers (quick reference):
- Purchase <= $1,000: Requester + Manager approval (Procurement team notified).
- $1,001–$10,000: Manager + Finance reviewer (PO required).
- > $10,000: Manager + Finance + VP-level sign-off + Legal review for vendor contracts.

Procurement workflow:
1. Complete Purchase Requisition form (link in header). Include justification, GL code, budget owner.
2. Finance validates budget and issues PO for approved requests.
3. Vendor invoices to be directed to procurements@redwood.com with PO number.

Corporate card & expense policy highlights:
- Cardholders must reconcile monthly. Attach receipt PDFs for any charge > $25.
- Personal expenses are prohibited. Card use for travel and subsistence only unless preapproved.
- Missing receipt: manager signoff + lost-receipt affidavit.

Expense coding examples (for AP):
- Travel: GL 6001.
- Contractor services: GL 5202.
- Cloud infra: GL 6105.

5) Vendor Onboarding & Ongoing Governance
Onboarding steps (minimum):
1. Initiation: Requester submits Vendor Onboarding Form including SOW, security questionnaire, and expected spend.
2. Procurement review: Finance validates budget and PO terms.
3. Security assessment: security team runs the Vendor Risk Questionnaire (VRQ). High-risk vendors require a full security assessment and a SOC2 or equivalent.
4. Legal review: contract terms, SLAs, liability clauses.
5. Account provisioning: least-privilege accounts issued and a named owner assigned.
6. Go-live: monitor first 30 days and schedule a 90-day checkpoint.

Vendor risk tiers and controls:
- Low: non-production SaaS with no sensitive data. Controls: standard contract + annual review.
- Medium: services that process internal data. Controls: VRQ, annual questionnaire, limited access scopes.
- High: vendors that handle regulated data or critical infrastructure. Controls: SOC2, penetration test evidence, quarterly reviews, contractual security SLAs, right-to-audit clause.

Termination checklist (vendors):
- Disable accounts and revoke keys.
- Verify data deletion or return per contract.
- Ensure final invoice & PO closure.
- Update asset & vendor registry.

6) Travel & Remote Work Expense Guidance
Pre-approval:
- All international travel requires manager + people-ops pre-approval.
- Travel estimated > $2,500 requires VP-level sign-off.

Travel booking & per diem:
- Book through corporate travel portal. Use preferred vendors where available.
- Per diem for meals: $75/day domestic, $100/day international (or actuals with receipts).

Safety & compliance:
- Employees traveling to high-risk regions must check-in with People Ops and register with the travel security provider.
- For work requiring visas or formal letters of invitation, allow 4–6 weeks lead time.

Expense submission timeline:
- Expenses must be submitted within 30 days of trip completion. Exceptions require manager approval.

7) Internal Templates & Quick Checklists
A. Access Request checklist (copy into Access Portal):
- Reason for access
- Resources requested (list)
- Duration (start/end)
- Business sponsor + Manager name
- Data categories involved
- Approval evidence uploaded

B. Vendor Onboarding templated fields (YAML example):
---
vendor_name: ""
vendor_type: "" # SaaS / Contractor / Hardware
estimated_annual_spend: ""
data_access: "" # none / internal / regulated
security_documents: ["SOC2", "PenTest"]
owner: ""
---

C. Change RFC minimum sections:
- Summary
- Owner & stakeholders
- Risk assessment
- Rollout plan & canary metrics
- Rollback procedure
- Schedule & maintenance window

D. Expense submission template (email subject):
Expense: <Your Name> - <Trip/Reason> - <MM/YYYY> | PO: <PO# if applicable>

8) Ownership & Escalation Matrix
Summary of primary owners:
- Access control operations: Security (IAM team)
- Change approval board: SRE + Platform leads + Product
- Procurement: Finance + Procurement ops
- Vendor risk & contracts: Legal + Security
- Travel & People Ops: People Ops + Finance

Escalation steps:
1. Attempt resolution with the owner.
2. If unresolved in 48 hours, escalate to team manager.
3. If unresolved in 5 business days or high-risk, escalate to Director-level.

- Access Portal: https://internal.redwood.com/access-portal

aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=ConsoleLogin --start-time 2025-01-01 --end-time 2025-06-01 --output json > login-audit.json
